evidence.rationale: The listing establishes identity well: the VIN decodes to a 2006 Cayman S 3.4, a Porsche COA is provided, the 6-speed manual and PASM are stated, and the title is clean (MT). It also discloses a Carfax-reported 'minor' front damage event in February 2025, for which the seller has no photos or repair details. Observed defects are cosmetic but numerous: a gash at the passenger rear wheel well, curb rash on two wheels, cracked aged PPF, a door paint stain, roof dings and creased leather. Service evidence is thin. The Carfax shows an alignment at 91,156 miles. The October 2026 oil service is claimed without documentation. The seller has no clutch replacement records. None of the model-critical items is shown: no borescope, no DME over-rev report, and no cooling/AOS/water-pump invoices on the M97 3.4, the engine with the higher bore-scoring exposure. Recent high-mileage S comps sold at $22.5k-$28.25k against a $23.6k-$28.6k fair value. The reserve and the remaining hammer are open. The full Carfax, gallery and videos were not captured here and may answer some of these questions.
evidence.next_action: Ask the dealer today to permit a Pasadena-area Porsche-specialist PPI with a borescope and DME over-rev report before the October 30 close, and to send the full Carfax PDF.
